theme: Airbnb pricing tools and dynamic-pricing repos that embed market data (PriceLabs, Beyond, Wheelhouse style; open-source STR pricing with comps)
queries_run: site:github.com pricelabs airbnb pricing data (WebSearch budget exhausted before this ran)
airbnb dynamic pricing tool open source github market data csv (WebSearch budget exhausted before this ran)
short term rental pricing open source github comps dataset (WebSearch budget exhausted before this ran)
github.com/search?q=rabbu OR mashvisor OR alltherooms (rate-limited, 1hr cooldown)
kaggle.com/search?q=airbnb dynamic pricing (JS-rendered, no results returned)

candidates.name: pricelabs-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/FastAPI/SQLite tool that, given a user's own PriceLabs API key, takes daily snapshots for a listing: recommended/base price and min-max cap flags, >20% price-change history, YoY booking pace (occupancy and revenue vs. same days-out last year, alerts at >10pp lag), 'neighborhood market comp' snapshots daily, 3 years of backfilled reservation history, and Airbnb/Booking.com channel-mix split. MIT licensed, 1 commit, 0 stars (low adoption/no track record). No sample data committed; requires the operator's own paid PriceLabs account to run.
candidates.why_useful: This is the most direct hit on the theme: a working, open-source method for pulling PriceLabs' own market-comp and pacing data (the exact quantity gap #2 wants — realised/ comp occupancy and ADR for STRs from a market-data vendor) rather than another NYC-2019 rehash. Would need a team member's/partner's PriceLabs subscription to actually run.
candidates.geography: whatever market the operator's PriceLabs listing/market is in (configurable)
candidates.time_coverage: point-forward snapshots from first run; 3yr reservation backfill
candidates.size_hint: no data committed; SQLite grows daily per listing tracked
candidates.last_activity: recent (2026, exact date not shown), 1 commit

candidates.name: airdnascraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapy-based scraper (airdna.py, scrapy.cfg) with a committed output file airdna.csv: title, room_type, property_type, bedrooms, accommodates, bathrooms, reviews, rating, days_available, occ, revenue for a small set of listings in the NJ lake region (Hopatcong/Cranberry Lake/Sparta/Newton area). occ and revenue columns are blank/'permission_denied' in the sample rows shown, so the financially useful fields are not actually populated.
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a scraping method aimed at AirDNA-hosted market pages (gap #2: realised ADR/occupancy for STRs), but the committed sample data is tiny, single-region, and missing exactly the occupancy/revenue fields that would matter; only the method (and its failure mode) is worth noting.
candidates.geography: New Jersey lake region (Hopatcong, Cranberry Lake, Sparta, Newton)

candidates.name: airdna-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python package (src/airdna_api/, pyproject.toml) that appears to be a client wrapper for AirDNA's paid API. 16 commits, 2 stars. No sample data or field documentation visible; requires a paid AirDNA account/API key to use.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made client for pulling AirDNA (realised ADR/occupancy comp data, gap #2) if the team ever gets AirDNA access; saves building a wrapper from scratch, but delivers nothing without a paid subscription.
candidates.geography: whatever AirDNA market the operator queries

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: dbt/Snowflake data-warehouse project (create_warehouse.sql, extract.py, kaggle_data.py, listings.py, load.py) that stitches together Inside Airbnb listing data (CC0), a Kaggle world-cities-population dataset, and a Kaggle cost-of-living-index dataset into a star schema, described as covering 'over 35 million records from 2015-2020' across global cities, with Metabase dashboards on top. 68 commits, 2 open PRs. No committed CSV/parquet data files were visible in the directory listing seen (extract.py presumably pulls from Inside Airbnb's own CDN/URLs at run time) — since Inside Airbnb's CDN no longer serves 2015-2020 vintages, re-running this pipeline today would likely NOT reproduce the historical 2015-2020 coverage the README claims unless the author's original run captured URLs that are since gone.
candidates.why_useful: If the extract.py source URLs or any cached intermediate files still resolve to older Inside Airbnb dump snapshots (worth a follow-up check), this could be a lead on gap #1 (pre-2023 Inside Airbnb dumps archived somewhere). As-is it is a pipeline definition, not a data cache, so treat as medium-low until verified whether it holds/points to actual archived dumps.
candidates.geography: global cities (Inside Airbnb coverage as of ~2020)
candidates.size_hint: claimed 35M+ records (in Snowflake, not committed to repo)
candidates.license: underlying data CC0; repo license not confirmed
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possible overlap/superset of our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel if the 2015-2020 vintages are real and recoverable

candidates.name: airbnb-scraper (everythingscraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client wrapping a paid Apify Actor that live-scrapes airbnb.com listing pages to compute STR underwriting metrics: 12-month forward occupancy rate, ADR, RevPAR, full day-by-day 12-month booking calendar, plus listing/host/amenity/review metadata. No historical data stored in the repo; live-pull only, priced per listing ($0.005/listing) via a third-party paid service.
candidates.why_useful: A working method to derive occupancy/ADR/RevPAR comps directly from Airbnb calendars at scale (gap #2/#8-style comp data), but it operates by scraping airbnb.com itself — squarely the class of tool CONTEXT flags as a terms-of-service decision for a human, so this should be catalogued as method-only and NOT run.

candidates.name: airbnb-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: Model Context Protocol server exposing two read-only tools that scrape live airbnb.com search results and listing detail pages (price with breakdown/discounts, ratings, host/Superhost status, amenities, address) as structured JSON via a paid hosted service (5 credits/call, 1,000 free credits/month). No committed dataset; configuration/documentation only.
candidates.why_useful: Another live airbnb.com scraping method (price + listing detail), same ToS caveat as above; only useful if a human explicitly clears scraping airbnb.com directly, which CONTEXT says to treat as out of bounds absent that decision.

candidates.name: awesome-billing
candidates.what_it_holds: Large (1.3k star) curated awesome-list on billing/payments/pricing knowledge for platforms; general SaaS pricing, not travel/STR specific. Listed here only because it surfaced under the 'pricing-strategy' topic search; no STR/Airbnb content confirmed.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — flagged only as a breadcrumb in case its pricing-strategy sub-sections link out to hospitality revenue-management resources; not independently verified to contain anything ABNB-relevant.

notes: Modality was badly constrained: the shared session WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout's first query ran, so none of the three planned WebSearch calls returned results — every finding here came from WebFetch against GitHub topic pages (which render server-side and worked) and the GitHub /search?q=... repo-search endpoint (which 429'd repeatedly and eventually returned a 1-hour Retry-After, so most planned repo-search queries could not run at all). DuckDuckGo HTML search and Kaggle/HuggingFace search pages returned CAPTCHA/JS-shell content that WebFetch could not read, so those hosts are effectively unusable for this kind of query with the current tools. Net result: PriceLabs, Beyond Pricing, and Wheelhouse itself have zero public GitHub repos (confirmed by visiting their orgs directly) — as expected, since these are commercial SaaS products, not open data. The theme's real yield is third-party client/scraper tooling around PriceLabs/AirDNA (pricelabs-tracker, airdna-api, airdnascraper) plus one ambiguous historical Inside-Airbnb aggregation pipeline (short-term-rentals-warehouse) whose 2015-2020 claim needs a follow-up repo clone/README read to confirm whether any of that vintage is actually recoverable from its extract scripts. A follow-up scout with a fresh WebSearch budget and either an authenticated GitHub session (to avoid the 429s) or wider spacing between /search calls would likely surface more — recommend re-running this exact theme once the session-wide WebSearch quota resets, and specifically checking github.com/topics/{wheelhouse,beyond-pricing,str-pricing,comp-set,revpar} which were not reachable this run, plus a direct README read of rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse's extract.py to see what URLs/date ranges it actually hits.
